concept: The scoreline is the shock, so the hero sets both totals in muted grey, 333 over 89, and lets the plain verdict ('India lose by 244 runs') land in white, backed by the margin and Henry's 6-27. Slides 2 and 3 are the two turning points as single giant numbers: 3 wickets in one over, 2 chances dropped in two balls. Slide 4 is the gut-punch chart: Will Young's 125 runs as one bar against India's whole team at 89, with the other scores beneath for scale, so the gap is seen before it is read. Slide 5 reframes it: India still lead 2-1 and Sunday decides the series. Cricket blue, type and bars only, no photos or logos.
caption:
New Zealand 333. India 89. A 244-run defeat at Mount Maunganui.

It was over almost before it began. Matt Henry, back after missing the first three games, removed Rohit, Kohli and Iyer in his first over, none of them scoring, and finished with a career-best 6 for 27.

The other turning point came in the morning: Will Young was dropped twice in two balls on 5, then made 125 off 108. On his own he outscored India's entire XI. Ishan Kishan's 27 was India's best.

India still lead 2-1, and the 5th ODI is on Sunday at the same ground. Series win, or does New Zealand level it 2-2? Tell us below.
